components.gap: The success condition requires this entry's definitions to be supplied and the identified source variants to be preserved. The entry defines only the expected logarithmic loss L_p(q) of a report on a single finite outcome set (body 444-450). It then asserts that 'the cumulative conditional logarithmic score is -log m_n(x_{1:n})' (body 457-459) without ever defining that score. Neither the per-outcome loss -log q(y) nor its sum over the conditional predictive factors r_i is stated, and the proof (annex 576-578) silently identifies the score with -sum_i log r_i. Within the unit's required source extent (Kass-Raftery Secs. 3.1-3.2), held text lines 293-297 and 355-367 (p. 777) define the logarithmic score as log pr_i(y_i), with overall score LS = sum_i log pr_i(y_i) = log pr(D|H_k) and log B_10 = LS_1 - LS_0. That is the opposite sign. The entry neither adopts that presentation nor identifies that it reverses it, so a required definition is missing and the source variant is not preserved.
